paragraphs: Azaryah. (Azaryah, king of Judah, II Kings 14:21.) Hyman cites Zohar Chadash, Ruth, at פ״א. In the consulted text, Rabbi Azaryah asks Rabbi Yose of Kefar Ono a question.
Hyman suggests that this may be R’ Azaryah, whom he cites from the end of Pirkei DeRabbi Eliezer, chapter 28, for the teaching that these kingdoms were created only as firewood for Gehinnom.

notes.text: The brief Zohar Chadash clause does not securely resolve who asked whom; the locator פ״א is also left in its supplied form. The proposed identification with the Azaryah of Pirkei deRabbi Eliezer remains tentative.

The brief ששאל clause does not securely decide whether Azaryah asks Yose of KefarOno or Yose asks him. No matching whole paragraph was supplied here. Earlier blanket claims that ZoharChadashRuth is unavailable are too broad: material was located under ZoharChadash, MidrashRut for another entry, not this question. Supplied פ״א remains literal and edition-dependent. IIKings14:21 is a namesake pointer, not identity with the rabbinic figure. PirkeiDeRabbiEliezer end28 and its ONLY/firewood saying remain Hyman’s perhaps identification; uninspected titles stay R'.

In the consulted Zohar Chadash, Midrash Rut 294, Azaryah asks Yose why sorcery is more common among women than among men. This locates the exchange without resolving Hyman’s edition numbering. The consulted Pirkei DeRabbi Eliezer 28 attributes the firewood saying to Rabbi Zeira. Earlier in the same chapter, Rabbi Elazar ben Azaryah speaks about the duration of the kingdoms’ rule. Hyman’s identification remains tentative.
